answer: Surety markets, not registries, do the work. Before transacting, an identity must be underwritten by an independent insurer posting capital against its fraud; the premium is set from verified history, so a fresh shell pays the maximum rate, and insurers refuse correlated books, leaving a farm to buy n policies at that rate. Each policy ties up the insurer's own capital, so covering a thousand siblings means a thousand exposures. Identity becomes a liability someone must be paid to carry: a wander through a canyon where every velvet rope is rented, never owned.
